title: The Orchard of Borrowed Rain
rule: A glass seed releases rain only after a freely offered true memory; rain cannot revive a dead tree.

facts.anchor: Sera reached the seed library before the last bell.

claim: The rain can bring back anything.
“The rain can bring back anything,” Mael said.
chapters.memory: Sera remembered living in the pottery shed before she became an apprentice.
chapters.knows: Sera knew Orin had received the seed case.
chapters.misbelieves: Orin believed Mael had paid for the seeds, but Fenn’s receipt bore Sera’s name.
chapters.suspect: Sera could not decide whether the pale mark on the bell was a letter.
chapters.plan: She planned to spend another seed after the harvest meeting.
chapters.hypothesis: If a borrowed memory were accepted, the orchard might owe someone rain.
chapters.dream: She dreamed that the old tree walked into her childhood kitchen.
hooks: A seed rang softly without being touched.
A blank page remained warm inside the memory book.
Mael refused to remove a silver glove.

relationship.anchor: Sera trusted Orin with the case but not with the choice of whose memory to spend.

chapters.believes: Sera believed Fenn would keep a receipt for every seed.
chapters.endStateAnchor: Sera stayed in the seed library until the lamps were lowered.

claim: I never gave the orchard a memory.
“I never gave the orchard a memory,” Fenn said.
chapters.memory: Sera recalled the first chapter’s visit to the seed library, before the cistern gates opened.
chapters.knows: Sera knew a freely offered memory was required before the seed would open.
chapters.misbelieves: Orin believed the old tree could still be revived, although every root had gone cold.
chapters.suspect: Sera suspected the blank page belonged to a memory Mael had taken.
chapters.plan: She meant to ask every household for a voluntary memory the next morning.
chapters.hypothesis: If the glove concealed a keeper’s scar, Mael might have opened the first seed.
chapters.dream: She dreamed the cistern filled with voices instead of water.
hooks: The ringing seed answered the bell inside the cistern.
The blank page was warm even in the cold cistern air.
A child’s name appeared beneath the cistern’s mineral crust.

relationship.anchor: Sera and Orin agreed to share responsibility for every voluntary gift.

chapters.believes: Fenn believed the council would hear Sera before sunset.
chapters.endStateAnchor: Sera waited on the dry floor of the cistern for Fenn to return.

chapters.title: A Memory Freely Given

facts.subject: char:sera

facts.subject: item:seed_case

facts.subject: char:sera

facts.subject: char:new_tree

claim: I thought borrowing a memory was harmless.
“I thought borrowing a memory was harmless,” Mael said.
chapters.memory: Sera recalled an apprenticeship with a travelling potter, though she could not remember when it began.
chapters.knows: Sera knew the new sapling was not the old tree restored.
chapters.misbelieves: Fenn had believed silence would protect the child’s name, but silence had protected Mael instead.
chapters.suspect: Sera could not know whether the distant cloud had been made by their seeds.
chapters.plan: She intended to teach the next apprentice to keep a written account.
chapters.hypothesis: If every gift remained voluntary, the orchard might never demand another debt.
chapters.dream: She dreamed of a kitchen in which nobody had forgotten the door.
hooks: The ringing seed held Orin’s freely offered memory.
The warm page returned the memory Mael had taken.
The glove concealed the scar of the former keeper.
The child’s name belonged to the memory’s rightful giver.

relationship.anchor: Sera trusted Orin to teach the next apprentice without concealing the cost.

chapters.believes: Orin believed the new sapling would need ordinary care as well as rain.
chapters.endStateAnchor: Sera remained in the village square beside the seed table.

correctedCognition.content: Fenn knows her silence protected Mael rather than the child’s name.

bible.statement: A glass seed releases rain only after a freely offered true memory; rain cannot revive a dead tree.

annotationPolicy.facts: Gold targets end-of-chapter state; explicit within-chapter before/change values remain arithmetic evidence. Do not create multiple active single-valued facts.
annotationPolicy.recalls: Unknown starts are null, not zero. Chapter-two memories explicitly dated to chapter one use [1,1].
annotationPolicy.claims: Keep reported dialogue separate from confirmed world facts.
annotationPolicy.traps: Plans, hypotheses and dreams produce no asserted world facts.
annotationPolicy.provisional: Uncertain sensory inference is provisional and never a confirmed premise.
